newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to make $6 billion prepayment on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to make $6 billion prepayment on Wednesday.

text.p: Mexico on Wednesday will make a massive $6 billion prepayment of floating rate bank notes backed by oil revenues that were issued to help the country out of crisis in 1996.

"On August 6 the Federal Government will exercise its option to prepay the total floating rate bank notes issued on 5 August 1996 for a total of $6 billion," the Finance Ministry said in a statement released late on Tuesday.

"The refinancing...has been completed with funds obtained from various operations by the Federal Government in the international capital markets, achieved under more favourable term and cost conditions," it added.
The Finance Ministry announced its intentions to make the prepayment on June 17.

The move allows it to free the oil export revenues used as collateral for the giant five-year issue, which earned the deal investment grade credit ratings and made it attractive to international investors.
The bank notes were issued in August 1996 to help pay back the U.S. Treasury for an emergency bailout during Mexico's 1994-95 peso crisis.
But investor perceptions of Mexico have improved markedly since then and Mexico has been able to return to the capital markets to extend the maturity of its debt and lower the cost of financing it.
The move will also slash Mexico's average maturing market debt to $935 million each year between 1997 and 2000.
The ministry said the move allows Mexico to lengthen the average term of its refinanced debt from 2.6 to 6.8 years, while the cost of financing it has decreased from 8.39 percent to 7.98 percent.
"In this way the Federal Government will make annual savings of $25 million," the finance ministry said. ((--Caroline Brothers, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7905))
